labels.label: prop:Cauchy_point_min
findings: ETT.tex:2303-2304, proof of prop:Cauchy_point_min: 'Proposition prop:C_connexe then shows that c_n is entirely contained in C_1'. This is the one ETT step that uses the gluing compactness. The inference does not hold as topology, even when both halves of prop:C_connexe hold. Counterexample: Causal.Gluing.expGluing_not_subset_correspondingLeft, two copies of R^2 glued along (a, c) -> (a, e^c) and the identity on (0,∞) × R. There C_1 = {0} × (0,∞) is open in ∂j1(N) (its trace on the upper half-plane), the corresponding pairs are closed, and the segment {0} × [0,1] of ∂j1(N) is connected, meets C_1 and is not contained in it. The inference does hold under the property: if the corresponding points stay locally in a compact set and C_1 is open in ∂j1(N), then a preconnected subset of ∂j1(N) that meets C_1 lies in C_1 (CorrespondingCompact.subset_correspondingLeft_of_isPreconnected). This sharpens the curation's paper_finding on prop:C_connexe ('does not follow ... without keeping the partners q in a compact set'). Nothing changes for the row: its Lean anchor Causal.CBG.ett_cauchy_point_min proves the proposition by another route (IsCorrPair.exists_corresponds_of_le). This file does not settle whether the step holds in ETT's geometric setting.

kb_proposals: The gluing compactness of DEC-160 is Causal.Gluing.CorrespondingCompact j₁ j₂ (CausalScaffold.GluingCompact; X side, Y side = CorrespondingCompact j₂ j₁). It is Iff.rfl to the inline hypothesis of isClosed_nonHausdorffLeft_of_isCompact. For weakly locally compact X it is properness of the projection of correspondingPairs onto X (correspondingCompact_iff_isProperMap). State new gluing theorems with it, not with the inline ∀-form.

A continuous extension of j₂ ∘ j₁⁻¹ across every corresponding boundary point does not give CorrespondingCompact. The exponential gluing has one and lacks the property (expGluing_continuous_extension_witness). correspondingCompact_of_continuousOn needs the continuous map near every point of closure C, so it cannot be read as 'A3 implies the property'.
notes: For the keeper (T-lad-gluing-nodes). NAME AND SIGNATURE: Causal.Gluing.CorrespondingCompact {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} {W : Type w} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (j₁ : W → X) (j₂ : W → Y) : Prop. It is defined as ∀ x ∈ frontier (range j₁), ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ K : Set Y, IsCompact K ∧ ∀ x' ∈ V, ∀ y, IsCorrespondingBoundaryPair j₁ j₂ x' y → y ∈ K. Its arguments are the gluing datum only: no topology on W, no open-embedding hypothesis, no causality. tools/ladder.py's index reads it as explicit binders ['j₁ : W → X', 'j₂ : W → Y'] and type Prop, once it is graduated under Causal/ (checked by running _lean_index on a copy). Its sort is none of causality, geometry or pair; T-lad-gluing-nodes already says this. In words: as the points of ∂ j₁(W) converge in X, their corresponding points in ∂ j₂(W) cannot escape every compact set of Y. WHAT IMPLIES IT: no corresponding pair at all (correspondingCompact_of_forall_not), hence any Hausdorff gluing along open embeddings (correspondingCompact_of_t2Space); ∂ j₂(W) compact (correspondingCompact_of_isCompact_frontier), hence Y compact (correspondingCompact_of_compactSpace); X locally compact and the correspondence a continuous map near every point of closure C (correspondingCompact_of_continuousOn); for X weakly locally compact, properness of the projection of the corresponding pairs onto X (correspondingCompact_iff_isProperMap, an iff). WHAT IT IMPLIES: the projection of the corresponding pairs onto X is proper (CorrespondingCompact.isProperMap, no hypothesis) and closed (CorrespondingCompact.isClosed_image_fst); Sbierski's C is closed (isClosed_correspondingLeft_of_correspondingCompact, no hypothesis); Chruściel's H is closed (isClosed_nonHausdorffLeft_of_correspondingCompact, T2 X, T2 Y, open embeddings); on both sides, the non-Hausdorff points of the gluing are closed (isClosed_nonHausdorffPoints_of_correspondingCompact); with C open in ∂ j₁(W), every preconnected subset of ∂ j₁(W) meeting C lies in C (CorrespondingCompact.subset_correspondingLeft_of_isPreconnected, the step at ETT.tex:2303); for a family with locally finite boundaries, the non-Hausdorff points seen in each piece are closed (FamilyGlueData.isClosed_preimage_ι_nonHausdorffPoints). WITNESSES: the property holds, with a corresponding pair, on the line with two origins (correspondingCompact_lineTwoOrigins; its non-Hausdorff points are closed, isClosed_nonHausdorffPoints_lineTwoOrigins). It fails, and H is not closed, on the exponential gluing (not_correspondingCompact_expGluing, expGluing_witness, where the pair form holds). The Y side holds there (correspondingCompact_expGluing_swap), so neither side implies the other. It fails while H is closed on the shear gluing (shearGluing_witness), so it is strictly stronger than the closedness of H. A continuous extension at every point of C does not give it (expGluing_continuous_extension_witness). This weighs against the T-lad-gluing-nodes evidence's 'compactness then from A3's continuous extension' read as topology; whether it holds in the CBG setting is open. GRADUATION: the module imports only Causal.GluingHausdorff and edits no existing file. Every name was grepped and none collides in Causal/, scaffold/ or lean-gx. Lines over 100 characters: only the two hypothesis-checklist table rows of the docstring, as in Causal/GluingHausdorff.lean.
